name: What AI is
strandNote: Optional for every quant role. For machine learning research roles, and for using and building AI tools with judgement.
description: See how a machine learns from examples: fit a line by nudging, build a neuron by hand and write text by counting.

requires.why: A model is a function machine whose rule is found from a table of examples.
Fits a line y = mx + c by changing its slope and its starting value.
Squares each error and uses powers to score a line.
The mean squared error is a mean, the average taught there.
The script uses loops and functions to nudge the weights until the error stops falling.
Turns counts into chances by dividing by the total, as that lesson does.

lessonNames.l3-learning-a-rule: Learning a rule from a table
lessonNames.l11-and-or: AND and OR from one neuron
lessonNames.l12-xor-needs-two: Why XOR needs a second layer

lessonObjectives.l1-rules-or-examples: Tell a program written as rules from a model learned from examples.
lessonObjectives.l2-features-and-labels: Name the features and the label in a table of examples.
lessonObjectives.l3-learning-a-rule: Choose the threshold that fits a table of examples best, and score it by how many it gets right.
lessonObjectives.l4-unseen-questions: Score a model on examples it was not fitted on, and say why a perfect score on its own examples proves little.
lessonObjectives.l5-how-wrong: Measure the errors of a line on a table of points, and see why we square them.
lessonObjectives.l6-mean-squared-error: Compute the mean squared error of a line by hand.
lessonObjectives.l7-nudge-and-keep: Improve one weight by trying a small nudge each way and keeping the better one.
lessonObjectives.l8-a-script-that-learns: Write a script that fits a line by nudging two weights until the error stops falling.
lessonObjectives.l9-weighted-vote: Compute a neuron's weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias.
lessonObjectives.l10-firing-or-not: Apply a threshold to the weighted sum and read the neuron's output as yes or no.
lessonObjectives.l11-and-or: Choose weights and a bias that make one neuron compute AND, and then OR.
lessonObjectives.l12-xor-needs-two: Show that no single neuron computes XOR, and build it from two layers of neurons.
lessonObjectives.l13-what-comes-next: Build a next-word table by counting the pairs of words in a text.
lessonObjectives.l14-chances-for-the-next-word: Turn a row of next-word counts into probabilities that add up to 1.
lessonObjectives.l15-writing-by-rolling-dice: Generate text by picking each next word from its probabilities with a random number.
lessonObjectives.l16-temperature-and-tokens: Change the temperature by raising probabilities to a power, and split text into tokens.
